titleStmt.title: Telegram From the Department of State to the Embassy in Venezuela

div.head: 484. Telegram From the Department of State to the Embassy in Venezuela
div.p: 2. Summary. As expected (Caracas 9556), President Lusinchi used President Reagan’s September 26 pull-aside to comment on Peru’s plight. Lusinchi also expressed concern for Haiti. The Venezuelan Chief Executive, in a talkative mood, commented on U.S. elections, Venezuelan elections, changes in the Soviet Union and his travels to Eastern Europe. Given the nature of the encounter—a reception—President Reagan did not respond to any specific points and there were no action implications. End summary.

3. President Reagan took President Lusinchi aside at a U.S.-hosted reception for heads of delegation attending UNGA to tell him that he was a bulwark for the cause of democracy in a key Latin American country. Lusinchi assured President Reagan that the transition period in Venezuela would be uneventful. Lusinchi described Carlos Andres Peres (CAP), his likely successor, as a strong anti-communist. Comment: Lusinchi clearly sought to assure the USG of the GOV’s continued interest in exercising regional leadership and in cooperating with the U.S. End comment.

4. Lusinchi manifested his interest in the region’s fledgling democracies by discussing Alan Garcia. The Secretary, also present, said Garcia had squandered a good opportunity to help his country at the beginning of his
administration. Lusinchi admitted that Garcia was immature, but insisted there were no alternatives; we should support Garcia. Lusinchi said that Venezuelan military leaders were in contact with their Peruvian counterparts at the request of Garcia.

5. Haiti was another topic of concern for Lusinchi. He said Avril was a good man and, again, urged U.S.-Venezuelan cooperation in Haiti. Lusinchi expressed specific concern for Haitian exile communities in Venezuela and Cuba. Comment: We note that Lusinchi’s positive disposition to Avril contrasts with the views of other Venezuelans (Caracas 10081), who are reserving judgment on the September 17 coup. End comment.
6. Ref B. responds to Ref. A points not discussed above.

note.p: Source: Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880935–0429. Confidential; Immediate. Sent for information to Maracaibo, Lima, Port-au-Prince, and the Interest Section in Havana. Drafted by Yale; cleared in NSC, ARA/AND, ARA, CAR, CCA, P, S/S, and S/S–O; approved by Abrams.

In telegram 10236 from Caracas, October 14, Reich wrote to Abrams requesting a readout of Reagan’s conversation with Lusinchi and a September meeting between Herrington and Venezuela Energy Minister Julio César Gil. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880918–0099)

In telegram 336400 to Caracas and the OPEC Collective, October 14, the Department reported on Gil’s September 28–29 meetings with Assistant Secretary of State for Economic and Business Affairs Eugene McAllister and Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Energy and Resources Policy John Ferriter: “Gil’s main message was Venezuela’s need for more foreign investment inflows and debt rescheduling to balance an expected 33 percent drop in oil revenues this year.” The Embassy also noted: “Reporting cable on Gil’s September 29 meeting with DOE Secretary Herrington is at DOE for clearance.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880916–0509)

In telegram 9556 from Caracas, September 23, the Embassy reported on Reich’s September 22 meeting with Lusinchi, who expressed serious concern about Peru. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880854–0448)

In telegram 10081 from Caracas, October 7, the Embassy sent an overview of Venezuelan views on the Avril coup in Haiti. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880899–0161)
